content:
Let \(a=x-6\) and \(b=7x-2\). Then
\[
ab=p^n,\qquad b=7a+40.
\]
Also
\[
\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(a,7a+40)=\gcd(a,40).
\]
If \(p\neq 2,5\), then \(p\nmid 40\), so \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). Since \(ab=p^n\), \(|a|\) and \(|b|\) must be powers of \(p\). If both were greater than \(1\), then \(p\) would divide both, contradicting \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). Thus one must be \(\pm1\).

Check:
- \(a=1\Rightarrow b=47\), so \(p=47\).
- \(a=-1\Rightarrow b=33\), product negative, impossible.
- \(b=\pm1\Rightarrow a=(b-40)/7\) not an integer.

Thus any prime solution other than \(2,5\) must be \(47\). Since \(47>5\), and \(x=7,n=1\) gives \(p=47\), the largest possible \(p\) is
\[
\boxed{47}.
\]
